title: Current (2026) AI has made game modding easier
author: Rajat_Sirkanungo
selftext: So, i was able to make another game mod for my single player game that i love (the game is called turbo overkill... you can find my mod on nexus if u are interested), and without this tech, it would have taken me at least a few days. I wanted ammo regeneration. The fact that i use AI/LLM even for my hobby and build satisfactory stuff with it tells me how the word "slop" to describe almost everything by AI is so uncharitable.

comments.author: Unfair-Frosting-4934
comments.body: exactly. People should be using AI like their own personal Jarvis and coming up with more personalized ideas or direct solutions to issue

comments.author: Sylvers
comments.body: Man, when TESVI releases, I expect half the mods to ever be made for it will be mostly AI assisted. The potential for lowering the barrier of entry on game mods is insane.

comments.author: clssaut
comments.body: The "slop" label is so reductive. Like, the output is only as meaningful as what you're trying to do with it, and using AI to build something you genuinely care about, for a game you love, is about as far from slop as it gets.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: Yes. AI is actually incredible for modding since it's able to operate in bite-sized chunks which is where AI shines (less likely to get confused/over-develop/duplicate/etc.) Honestly this is probably the way people should be building their games with in the first place (lightweight framework with 90% of the data in self-contained modules.)

comments.author: Civil_Log_7536
comments.body: This is probably the best use case for AI IMO. The idea comes from the person still but AI bridge the gap in between. Esp for hobby modding.
